eyebrow: Lesson 16 · B1 · Being a Good Guest · 20 câu
heading: Meals, Chats and Goodbyes
source: Bài đọc phỏng theo Being a Good Guest – Ann Ingalls (The Child's World, 2013), tr. 16–21.
credit: Tranh minh hoạ: Ronnie Rooney, trong Being a Good Guest (The Child's World, 2013). Dùng cho mục đích học tập.

paras.label: A
paras.text: If you are lucky, your friend's family may ask you to stay for a meal. Always wait to be {offered|offered} food; never {help yourself|help yourself} from the kitchen. When the meal is over, tell your host how delicious it was, carry your plate to the kitchen and offer to help with the {washing-up|washing-up}. It is a great way of saying "Thank you". In Turkey, asking for a second helping is even a {compliment|compliment} to the cook!

paras.label: B
paras.text: Talk to your friend's family too. Be polite, answer their questions and remember the {magic words|magic words}: "Please", "Thank you" and "Excuse me".

paras.label: C
paras.text: Be friendly, but try not to {get in the way|get in the way}. Everyone needs a bit of space. If your host starts {yawning|yawning}, it is probably time to go home, not time to describe every comic in your {collection|collection}!

paras.label: D
paras.text: When it is time to leave, thank your host. Once you are home, send a {thank-you note|thank-you note} saying how much fun you had.

paras.label: E
paras.text: Finally, {return the favour|return the favour}. Invite your friend to your house some time, and this time you can be the host. After all, good guests often make great hosts!

parts.title: Part 1 · Which paragraph?
parts.instr: Đoạn nào (A–E) chứa thông tin dưới đây?

items.label: A paragraph that mentions a country where asking for more food is polite
items.why: Đoạn A: Thổ Nhĩ Kỳ – xin thêm là lời khen.

items.label: A paragraph that lists some useful polite expressions
items.why: Đoạn B: *Please, Thank you, Excuse me.*

items.label: A paragraph that describes a sign that a visit should end
items.why: Đoạn C: chủ nhà ngáp → nên về.

items.label: A paragraph about something to do after you get home
items.why: Đoạn D: *Once you are home, send a thank-you note.*

items.label: A paragraph that suggests swapping roles with your friend
items.why: Đoạn E: lần này bạn làm chủ nhà.

parts.title: Part 2 · Reading comprehension
parts.instr: Chọn đáp án đúng hoặc True / False.

questions.q: According to (A), what should you do if you are hungry at a friend's house?
options: wait until the family offers you food
take a snack from the kitchen
questions.why: *Always wait to be offered food; never help yourself.*

questions.q: The writer suggests offering to help with the washing-up after a meal.
questions.why: Đúng. *offer to help with the washing-up.*

questions.q: In Turkey, why is asking for more food a good thing?
options: It shows the cook that the food was very good.
It means the guest is very hungry.
It is a way of saying goodbye.
It stops food from being wasted.
questions.why: *asking for a second helping is even a compliment to the cook.*

questions.q: The writer thinks you should show your host your whole comic collection.
questions.why: Sai. *not time to describe every comic in your collection!*

questions.q: What should you write in a thank-you note?
options: when you want to come back

questions.q: What does the last sentence of the text suggest?
options: Being a guest teaches you how to be a good host.
Hosts are better people than guests.
You should never invite friends home.

parts.title: Part 3 · Picture tasks
parts.instr: Quan sát tranh minh hoạ trong sách và trả lời.

questions.q: Which part of a visit does this picture show?
questions.why: Rửa bát → sau bữa ăn (đoạn A).
questions.alt: A girl stands beside a woman washing dishes in a sink full of bubbles and asks: May I help you with the dishes?

questions.q: Why does the boy in red decide to go home?
options: His friend is yawning and looks tired.
His friend asked him to leave.
questions.why: Đoạn C: *If your host starts yawning, it is probably time to go home.*
questions.alt: Two boys sit at a table; one yawns while the other says: I should go home. I will see you tomorrow.

questions.why: Viết thiệp cảm ơn → đoạn D.
questions.alt: A girl sits at a table writing a thank-you card

parts.title: Part 4 · Gapped text
parts.instr: Đọc đoạn văn ngắn và chọn câu phù hợp cho mỗi chỗ trống. Có 2 câu thừa.
parts.text: On Friday I had dinner at my friend Sam's house. [1] After dinner, Sam's mum started clearing the table. [2] At nine o'clock, Sam began to yawn. [3]
options: Sam's dad served us eggs and toast for breakfast.
His dad made a huge pot of spaghetti, and I told him it was the best I'd ever tasted.
I jumped up, carried my plate to the kitchen and offered to dry the dishes.
So we went to the cinema to watch a film about dinosaurs.
I realised it was time to go, so I thanked everyone and said goodbye.

items.why: Bữa tối + lời khen món ăn.
Mẹ Sam dọn bàn → mình giúp.

parts.title: Part 5 · Words in context
parts.instr: Đoán nghĩa của từ/cụm từ dựa vào ngữ cảnh.

questions.q: *…never help yourself from the kitchen* (A). To **help yourself** means to…
options: take something without waiting to be offered

questions.q: *…try not to get in the way* (C). If you **get in the way**, you…
options: stop others from doing what they want or need to do
questions.why: **Get in the way** = gây vướng víu.

questions.q: *Finally, return the favour* (E). To **return the favour** means to…
options: do something kind for someone who was kind to you
take a present back to the shop
questions.why: **Return the favour** = đáp lại lòng tốt.
